extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders preparing public comments on the 2026 CMS Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs proposed rule (payers, state Medicaid/CHIP agencies, QHP issuers, MA organizations, Medicaid managed care plans, CHIP entities, providers, PBMs, EHR and health IT vendors, app developers)
extracted.subtask_short: commenting on CMS interoperability/prior auth rule
extracted.subtask_description: A guide and template to help submit public comments to CMS on the 2026 proposed rule (CMS-0062-P) covering interoperability API standards and electronic prior authorization for drugs, including the specific proposals, compliance dates, exceptions, and targeted requests for comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support NCPDP standards for pharmacy-benefit electronic prior authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: State Medicaid and CHIP FFS programs, Medicaid managed care plans, CHIP managed care entities, and QHP issuers on the FFEs would be required to support an unexpired version of the NCPDP SCRIPT standard (transactions: PAInitiationRequest, PAInitiationResponse, PARequest, PAResponse, PAAppealRequest, PAAppealResponse, PACancelRequest, PACancelResponse, PANotification), an unexpired version of the NCPDP Formulary & Benefit (F&B) standard to make available formulary/benefits information, and an unexpired version of the NCPDP RTPB standard for real-time coverage information by October 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for comment include: how payers make F&B files available, update frequency for F&B and prior-authorization indicators, provider use and EHR integration of F&B and RTPB, accuracy of group-level information to specific patients, whether RTPB can indicate drugs covered under a medical benefit, whether RTPB could negate F&B, burden of requiring both standards, and other technical solutions to indicate how prior authorization should be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required FHIR standards for APIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Impacted payers would be required to implement and maintain API technology conformant with unexpired versions of the standards adopted in 45 CFR 170.215 (specifically subsections identified) beginning on the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS requests comment on opportunities to streamline by relying on use-case-specific IGs versus also requiring base FHIR, on possible alignment challenges when independently requiring multiple standards, and on whether CMS should more narrowly specify only particular capabilities of required IGs (example given: SMART App Launch capability subsets relevant to Patient Access API).

rubrics_metrics.name: Require additional Implementation Guides (IGs) for specific APIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Impacted payers would be required to use specified unexpired IGs by October 1, 2027: Patient Access (CARIN Blue Button, PDex, PDex US Drug Formulary IG); Provider Access (CARIN Blue Button, PDex); Provider Directory (PDex Plan Net IG); Payer-to-Payer (CARIN Blue Button, PDex); Prior Authorization (CRD IG, DTR IG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative proposal: require PDex US Drug Formulary IG for Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer if formulary data retained. Requests for comment ask whether recommended IGs are mature enough to require, how CMS can assess readiness, and whether to require FAST Security IG or CARIN RTPBC IG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend additional IGs (non-mandatory) to support APIs
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS recommends (not requires) certain IGs: FAST Security IG for Patient Access; ATR List IG and FAST Security IG for Provider Access; CDex IG and FAST Security IG for Prior Authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for comment on maturity/readiness of these IGs, whether and when to move recommendations to requirements, and potential burdens and testing needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate drugs covered under a medical benefit into the Prior Authorization API
rubrics_metrics.description: Impacted payers would be required to incorporate coverage and documentation requirements into the Prior Authorization API to support electronic prior authorization for drugs covered under a medical benefit by October 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for comment on whether the scope and rubric distinguishing drugs covered under medical vs pharmacy benefit (e.g., by claims processing system) is clear and appropriate across MA organizations, state Medicaid/CHIP FFS programs, and other payers, and whether supplemental benefits or other categories should be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and extension processes for small populations and certain payers
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove the 2024 policy allowing states with small FFS populations to request exemption for non-drug items/services PA API; allow state Medicaid and CHIP FFS programs to request extensions to implement the Prior Authorization API and incorporation of medical-benefit drugs; allow state Medicaid/CHIP FFS programs to request extensions and QHP issuers on the FFEs to request exceptions from required NCPDP standards support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed amendment to 45 CFR 156.223(i)(1)(iii) to require QHP issuers seeking exceptions to describe current/proposed means of conducting prior authorization. Request for comment on flexibilities to reduce burden while ensuring HIPAA transaction standards compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require providers be communicated a specific reason for denial for drug prior authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: State Medicaid and CHIP FFS programs, Medicaid managed care plans, CHIP managed care entities, and QHP issuers on the FFEs would be required to communicate to providers a specific reason for denying a prior authorization request for any drugs, regardless of transmission method, by October 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes structural readability changes to 42 CFR 438.210(c) and 42 CFR 438.242. No additional scoring guidance provided; CMS solicits comment on operational impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior authorization decision timeframes for QHP issuers on FFEs
rubrics_metrics.description: QHP issuers on the FFEs must notify requesting providers of prior authorization decisions 'as expeditiously as the enrollee's health condition requires' but no later than: 7 calendar days after receiving a standard prior authorization request for non-drug items and services; 72 hours after an expedited request for non-drug items and services; 72 hours after a standard prior authorization request for drugs; and 24 hours after an expedited request for drugs — all by October 1, 2027. QHP issuers may extend notification timeframes up to 14 calendar days under certain circumstances if they provide written reasons and inform providers of right to file expedited grievance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS requests comment on how to interpret 'as expeditiously...', whether additional regulatory or sub-regulatory language is needed, on potential burden of differing timeframes between provider vs patient notifications, whether to require shorter timeframes (e.g., 24 hours for all drug requests), and whether parent organizations can leverage experience from other lines of business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align decision timeframe requirements for certain drugs with existing 24-hour standard
rubrics_metrics.description: If commenters identify gaps, state Medicaid FFS programs, Medicaid managed care plans, and CHIP managed care entities would be required to provide notice of prior authorization decisions for drugs within a timeframe that aligns with the existing 24-hour decision timeframe for covered outpatient drugs requirements by October 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for comment on whether particular drug types should be included, and whether MA organizations should be required to respond to all drug requests within 24 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior authorization decision timeframes for prescription drugs for State CHIP FFS
rubrics_metrics.description: State CHIP FFS programs would be required to provide notice to providers and patients of prior authorization decisions as expeditiously as beneficiary's medical needs require but no later than 24 hours after receiving a prior authorization request for prescription drugs for which FFP is available, by October 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request for comment on scope and implementation considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update terminology for State Medicaid and CHIP FFS decision timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise regulatory language to explain that state Medicaid and CHIP FFS programs must make prior authorization decisions available for non-drug items and services no later than 7 calendar days for standard requests and 72 hours for expedited requests unless a shorter state timeframe exists, effective upon final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation guidance tied to regulatory text restructuring; CMS solicits comment on clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require reporting of prior authorization metrics for non-drug items and services (Medicaid managed care and CHIP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicaid managed care plans and CHIP managed care entities would be required to report certain metrics about prior authorizations for non-drug items and services, by program and by plan, no later than 90 days after the end of their contract rating period, beginning on the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metrics were finalized in the 2024 rule; CMS proposes changes to reporting deadlines and levels and requests comment on operational reporting mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require impacted payers to publicly report prior authorization metrics for drugs
rubrics_metrics.description: MA organizations, state Medicaid and CHIP FFS programs, Medicaid managed care plans, CHIP entities, and QHP issuers on the FFEs would be required to report prior authorization metrics for drugs on public websites beginning in 2028 (reporting 2027 periods). Deadlines: MA/state/QHP by March 31 for prior calendar year; Medicaid managed care/CHIP entities within 90 days after rating period. Reporting levels specified by payer type (contract, state, plan/program, issuer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request for comment on inclusion of drugs payable under Part A and other scope questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient Access API requirement for small-group FF-SHOP QHP issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: Small group market QHP issuers on the FF-SHOPs would be required to implement and maintain a Patient Access API conformant with individual-market FFEs requirements by January 1, 2028, and to annually report Patient Access API metrics to CMS beginning in 2029 (reporting 2028 period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS requests comment whether compliance date provides sufficient time given issuers often also offer individual market QHPs on FFEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider Access API requirement for small-group FF-SHOP QHP issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: Small group market QHP issuers on the FF-SHOPs would be required to implement and maintain a Provider Access API conformant with individual-market FFEs requirements by January 1, 2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS solicits comment on compliance date feasibility given common shared implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payer-to-Payer API requirement for small-group FF-SHOP QHP issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: Small group market QHP issuers on the FF-SHOPs would be required to implement and maintain a Payer-to-Payer API conformant with individual-market FFEs requirements by January 1, 2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS solicits comment on feasibility and burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Authorization API and process requirements for small-group FF-SHOP QHP issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: Small group market QHP issuers on the FF-SHOPs would be required to implement and maintain a Prior Authorization API conformant with individual-market FFEs requirements by January 1, 2028; respond to providers with a reason for denial for non-drug items/services by October 1, 2027; and publicly report prior authorization metrics on non-drug items/services beginning in 2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS requests comment on compliance date sufficiency given issuers' existing efforts for individual market QHPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply same exceptions process to small-group FF-SHOP QHP issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: Small group market QHP issuers on the FF-SHOPs would be subject to the same exceptions process currently applicable to individual-market QHP issuers on the FFEs per cited CFR provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No additional guidance; this is a parity proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require impacted payers to report API endpoints and documentation to CMS
rubrics_metrics.description: Impacted payers would be required to report all API endpoints to CMS in the form of an Endpoint Resource (FHIR) including appropriate use cases. They must also report URLs for API FHIR capability statement, authorization/authentication protocols and implementation details, and API registration information. Reporting due no later than 60 days after effective date of final rule; update CMS within one week of changes; verify at least once every 12 months; new payers report no later than 60 days before covering patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative proposal: report NDH IG Endpoint Profile resources instead. Requests for comment on whether direct URL to capability statement is necessary, whether single URL for auth/registration is sufficient, discrete data elements to collect, burdens of reporting, and best publication mechanisms (machine-readable file vs FHIR-enabled registry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Add prior authorization information for all drugs to Access APIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Impacted payers would be required to add information about prior authorization requests and decisions for all drugs to data made available through Patient Access, Provider Access, and Payer-to-Payer APIs within the timeframes established for non-drug items and services by October 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No additional guidance beyond the proposal; part of aligning Access APIs with prior authorization transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient Access API usage metrics reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicaid managed care plans and CHIP entities must report Patient Access API usage metrics to states by program and plan no later than 90 days after end of rating period; QHP issuers on FFEs must report Patient Access API usage metrics to CMS no later than the QHP certification application deadline for the subsequent year, beginning on the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for comment on timing, mechanisms, and burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report Provider Access, Payer-to-Payer, and Prior Authorization API usage metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Impacted payers would be required to report aggregated, de-identified metrics about usage of Provider Access, Payer-to-Payer, and Prior Authorization APIs beginning in 2028 (reporting 2027 period). Deadlines and reporting levels vary by payer type (calendar year March 31 for MA/state/QHP vs 90 days after rating period for managed care/CHIP). CMS does not plan to publicly report named payer/plan-level data but may publish aggregated/de-identified data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for comment on metric definitions, disaggregation (e.g., individual vs group providers; old->new vs concurrent payer exchanges), reporting mechanisms (APD process, online portal, FHIR server), and burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove drug formulary information from Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer APIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to remove drug formulary data as required data in Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer APIs for MA organizations, state Medicaid/CHIP FFS programs, Medicaid managed care plans, and CHIP entities beginning on the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request for comment on whether there are use cases that require formulary access via those APIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update denial/discontinuation policies for Provider Directory API
rubrics_metrics.description: MA organizations, state Medicaid and CHIP FFS programs, Medicaid managed care plans, and CHIP entities would be required to update their Provider Directory API denial or discontinuation policies beginning on the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No additional specifics provided in template; CMS signals requirement for updated policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate existing API applicability dates into regulatory text
rubrics_metrics.description: Restructure regulatory text to incorporate existing Patient Access API 2021 implementation date and the requirement to make available data with a date on or after January 1, 2016 into specified CFR sections, effective on final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is regulatory housekeeping to clarify applicability dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require QHP issuers applying for exceptions to describe impact of non-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend language to require QHP issuers on FFEs applying for an exception to describe the impact of non-compliance on all applicable parties beginning on the effective date of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This raises informational requirement for exception applications; CMS seeks comment on clarity and burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define 'failure to report' for Open Payments and authorize CMPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a definition of 'failure to report' in 42 CFR 403.902 allowing CMS to impose civil monetary penalties where applicable manufacturers or GPOs fail to grant timely access (within 30 calendar days of audit request) to books, contracts, records, documents, and other evidence sufficient to enable audit/inspection beginning on effective date of final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request for comment on definition and CMP application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify HIPAA standards related to prior authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals include defining prior authorization as certain transmissions described in 45 CFR 162.1301(a) and (c), modifying current operating rules associated with eligibility transactions to exclude prior authorization-related transmissions, and adopting specified FHIR specifications for eligibility and 'referral certification and authorization' transactions and for prior authorization attachments (CDex IG) with compliance dates 24 months from effective date (36 months for small health plans). Adopted specs listed (FHIR Release 4.0.1, US Core IG STU 6.1.0, SMART App Launch IG 2.0.0, CRD IG 2.2.1—STU 2.2, DTR IG 2.2.0—STU 2.2, PAS IG 2.2.1—STU 2.2; CDex IG v2.1.0—STU 2.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative: adopt FHIR standards for all referral certification/authorization transactions. Requests for comment on burden of maintaining both FHIR and X12N standards (e.g., X12N 278), whether to adopt later versions, whether to rely on HL7 Major.Minor.Patch approach, whether to recommend vs adopt CDex immediately, and phasing and compliance date interactions with attachments adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisit direct data entry exception under HIPAA
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS requests comment on whether to revisit the direct data entry exception in 45 CFR 162.923(b) to incentivize or require migration from portal-based transactions to fully electronic transactions using adopted standards, how amending/removing this exception would affect other standard transactions, types of entities affected, and possible burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions include which HIPAA covered entities and transaction types would be affected and whether amendment would perversely incentivize manual transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt standards for use by HHS and set expiration dates for older versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to adopt standards in 45 CFR 170.215(j), (k), (m), and (n) on behalf of the Secretary and to add an expiration date of January 1, 2028 to corresponding currently listed standards if newer versions are adopted. Alternative: remove and replace older versions without a transition period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS requests comment on transition approaches and impact of expiring older versions vs immediate replacement without transition.
